extra.reason: Socket client, reconnect/resubscribe, correlated requests, live capture script, and recorded fixtures all delivered and reviewed. Two acceptance criteria were amended by findings, both recorded as tests and notes on the affected tickets: (1) 'emits every one of the 26 event types' is 24 of 26 - pane_output_changed has no subscription of any kind and is unreachable, and pane_agent_status_changed is only offered per-pane and is unnecessary because pane_updated carries agent_status globally; (2) the fixture covers 15 of 26 kinds, with every absent kind enumerated and reason-coded in fixtures.test.mjs so a newly missing kind fails the suite.

Pin model retired and the reducer seam stands. All eight acceptance criteria met, including the profile, which the review initially found missing: a generated Stream Deck + XL profile now places both actions across all 36 keys and 6 encoders, declared against DeviceType 13, with tests asserting every coordinate is filled and no undeclared action is placed.

Two corrections were made to accepted decisions, both recorded in the ADRs and noted on -3rd: (1) an encoder and its touch-strip region are ONE control, so the XL has 42 addressable controls rather than 48, and setImage on a dial targets the Stream Deck app rather than the hardware; (2) the socket client's request path would have killed the event stream, since Herdr closes a connection after answering and a second request on the subscription connection takes the stream down with it.

Verified against a running Herdr: 93 events produced 3 snapshot reads and 6 control redraws after the initial paint. 71 tests, typecheck, preview, build, and streamdeck validate all pass.

Three workstream channels render live on the XL, each naming its workstream, its branch, and its aggregate agent state, verified end to end against a running Herdr (190 events -> 1 snapshot read, 1 worktree read, real branch and live status). All nine acceptance criteria met. Both review axes ran and both found real defects, all fixed in a02e2c2.

Two acceptance criteria rested on premises that are false of Herdr 0.8.0, both found by probing a live server rather than reading the schema, both recorded as notes here and corrected in ADR-0001 in place:

(1) 'Each channel shows ... aggregated agent state' was to be satisfied by consuming WorkspaceInfo.agent_status, which the description said Herdr 'already aggregates ... so this ticket consumes that rather than recomputing it'. Herdr NEVER PUSHES that field: 45 seconds on every global subscription produced 417 pane_updated events carrying 8 agent-status changes and ZERO workspace_updated. Only a snapshot re-read picks the aggregate up, and pane_updated is not structural, so nothing schedules one. Consuming it would have frozen every channel at whatever it was when something structural last happened - the exact opposite of criterion 4. The aggregate is recomputed from panes instead, counting only panes with a non-null agent, since a pane without one reports 'unknown' (4 of 5 live).

(2) 'Worktree-backed workspaces ... carrying repository, branch, and checkout path' cannot be met from the snapshot. WorkspaceWorktreeInfo has five fields and none is a branch; branch lives on WorktreeInfo, returned only by worktree.list. The reducer now issues one worktree.list per distinct repo_key - not per workstream, since one call answers for a whole repository - and a channel renders before the reply arrives.

Two deviations from accepted decisions are staged rather than resolved, and both are now recorded in the ADR they contradict rather than only in a code comment:

- ADR-0003 puts workstream identity on the strip regions, but this ticket's description defers the strip to -2gn. Identity therefore sits on each channel's top key row (HEADER_ROW in src/device/surface.ts), which costs -4bb a role row. Whichever of -2gn and -4bb lands second deletes HEADER_ROW and reclaims the row; both carry a note.
- ADR-0009 requires durable slot assignment. Channels currently take workstreams in workspace-number order, so a closing workstream slides the others left - the auto-fill ADR-0009 rejects. That is -77f's job and -77f holds a note naming the seam.

One known limit with no owner yet: a 'git switch' inside an existing worktree emits no Herdr event of any kind, so a branch changed from the terminal shows the old name until something else forces a snapshot. Recorded in ADR-0001; polling for it would undo ADR-0004.

Durable slot assignment, the enforced three-slot cap, and the live overflow count all land, verified end to end against a running Herdr. Eight of nine acceptance criteria fully met; one is partial and named below. Both review axes ran; the Spec axis found a real bug, fixed in 111a9fb.

THE BUG WORTH REMEMBERING: hold-to-release worked, and then the next snapshot handed the workstream straight back to the channel it had just been taken out of, because automatic assignment runs on every snapshot - many times a minute. The gesture was theatre. Slots therefore carry a  set: a workstream the developer takes off the device is passed over by automatic assignment until deliberately taken back, and is forgotten once it no longer exists. Anything that adds another automatic-assignment path must respect it.

PARTIAL - criterion 3, 'An unbound slot renders as an offer to create a worktree, and creating one binds it to that slot'. The offer renders (a numbered '+' reading NEW WORKTREE) and the binding half works for every case reachable today: a newly created worktree workspace takes the free channel, covered by the reducer test 'a worktree created while one channel is free lands in that channel'. What is NOT built is a key press that calls worktree.create, and with it the reservation that would bind a new worktree to the SPECIFIC channel pressed rather than the lowest free one. Firing an irreversible git command from a physical button with no branch name is not a one-line addition, and -8e8 ('Dial 2: create and remove worktrees from the device') owns the creation flow and is unblocked by this closure. -8e8 carries a note saying it must add the reservation rather than assume this ticket did.

ADR-0009 IS AMENDED IN PLACE, not quietly contradicted. It said slot assignment is 'a manual act'; building it showed that to be the wrong half. Assignment is automatic and sticky, REASSIGNMENT is the manual act. The concern the ADR actually rests on is that a workstream must never move, and a channel filled once that never reflows does not move. Requiring a manual act on top would buy no stability and leave a fresh install showing three empty channels.

Reassignment ended up as ONE rule rather than two, because the review showed a separate release and adopt could not choose which workstream a channel took. A hold on the channel's identity key moves that channel on to the next thing it could show; 'nothing' is always in the cycle, so a channel can always be cleared and holding repeatedly comes back round.

DURABLE KEY, probed rather than assumed: a worktree-backed workstream keys on checkout_path, which survives even Herdr losing its session file. A workspace with no worktree can only key on workspace_id - Herdr persists that verbatim in ~/.config/herdr/session.json, so it survives a restart but not a session reset. identity_cwd would be the better key but is not exposed on the socket at all. The two are prefixed so they cannot collide.

Known collision for -2gn: overflow occupies the rightmost strip region per ADR-0011, which is also channel 3's second encoder. -2gn holds a note.

138 tests, typecheck, preview, build, and streamdeck validate all pass.

The strip is a permanent instrument reading now: each channel's two regions carry its branch and its live readings, and the answer to "how is this stream doing" costs no input. Verified end to end against a running Herdr. Eight of nine criteria fully met, one partial and named below. Both review axes ran and both found real defects, all fixed in 636e8ae.

THE TWO REGIONS ARE ONE COMPOSITION, not two cards. The renderer draws the whole 400px block and each region is a window onto it, which is what lets a branch run past the seam instead of being cut in half at it. Both regions therefore describe the same block, and the projection decides what fits before the renderer draws anything.

THREE DEFECTS THE REVIEW FOUND, all of them the strip promising more than it delivered:

1. RESERVED SPACE WAS NOT RESERVED. Only the reading was held, not its width, so -wl7 filling TKT and PR in would have shoved AGENTS off - the opposite of the comment's claim. Readings now carry the width the layout sets aside whatever the value currently is. CONSTRAINT FOR -wl7: the layout can promise a pull request FOUR cells without costing the droppable reading, so its state must be said in four (OPEN, DRFT, or a number). Going wider is allowed and simply spends AGENTS.
2. CUTTING THE START TRADED ONE AMBIGUITY FOR ITS MIRROR. Keeping the tail saved feature/auth/rewrite from feature/auth/revert but merged alice/fix-login with bob/fix-login. A long branch now loses its MIDDLE, which is the only cut that survives either.
3. THE BRANCH WAS VISIBLE NOWHERE WHEN HERDR WAS DOWN, because the notice emptied every block and this same change had taken the branch off the keys. The branch stays now and only the counts go. Each channel carries its own notice, because a region only ever draws its own block - a central message was legible on one region out of six.

PARTIAL - criterion 8, "Reducer tests cover branch changes, count changes, and the unknown-enrichment state". All three states are covered, and a count change is proven to redraw only the affected channel's regions. What is NOT covered is a test asserting that a BRANCH change specifically redraws the strip; the redraw path is exercised through agent status instead. Cheap to add and worth adding with -wl7's tests.

SCOPE: no enrichment token name was invented - -5ot defines the contract, -wl7 reads it. Verified on live Herdr that WorkspaceInfo.tokens is literally null today, so the unknown is real rather than a placeholder.

TWO THINGS KEPT THAT WERE NOT ASKED FOR, both because dropping them would have been regressions: the whole-strip connection notice, which had no other home once the -2kw placeholder was replaced, and moving the branch off the header keys, which the NOTES on this ticket authorise and which frees one key per channel for -4bb.

THE TOUCH STRIP IS AN INPUT, newly established here: the SDK's touchTap carries both `hold` and `tapPos`. That is where -77f's slot-reassignment gesture should move when -4bb finally reclaims the header row, and it needs no timer of its own. Recorded on -4bb and in ADR-0003.

ADR-0003 and ADR-0007 both amended in place with what was built, the pixel arithmetic behind the budgets, and what -4bb still needs first.

162 tests, typecheck, preview, build, and streamdeck validate all pass.

Each channel now shows its workstream's panes on three role rows, with roles aligned across all three channels. Verified end to end against a running Herdr: the real agent on row 0 with its live status, four shells on row 2 as two keys and a count, and one process read per pane. Ten of eleven criteria met; one is asserted rather than observed and is filed. Both review axes ran and both found real defects, all fixed in 6bde173.

THREE THINGS ADR-0003 HAD WRONG ABOUT pane.process_info, each found by calling it on a running Herdr, two of which would have broken detection on the case that matters most. All three are corrected in the ADR.
1. `name` is not the program's name. The live agent pane reported name '2.1.233' - Claude's VERSION, because it rewrites its process title - with argv0 and cmdline both 'claude'. Matching on name would have failed to find the agent and would have keyed every role override to a release.
2. The first foreground process is the wrong one. That same pane listed an MCP server the agent had spawned BEFORE the agent itself, so taking foreground_processes[0] would have labelled the agent row an ebook indexer. foreground_process_group_id says which entry identifies the pane.
3. It is one request per pane, since the call takes a single nullable pane_id and null means the FOCUSED pane.
A fourth finding is about naming rather than detection: terminal_title_stripped is the most descriptive field Herdr offers and is unusable as a key label, because an agent rewrites its title as it works and the key would be renamed and redrawn every few seconds.

TWO REAL BUGS THE REVIEW FOUND, both now fixed:
- AGENT ROLES WERE PERMANENTLY UN-OVERRIDABLE. Agent panes were never asked about, since Herdr detects agents itself. True, but a role is corrected against a command line, so a pane never asked about could never be corrected - holding an agent key did nothing, for ever. Every pane is asked about now; Herdr's answer still decides the agent row.
- PROCESS INFO WAS CACHED FOR THE PANE'S LIFETIME. Killing a test watcher and starting a dev server in the same pane left it on the tests row until the pane closed. pane_exited now forgets what that pane was running.

A THIRD DEFECT I FOUND BY STRESS-TESTING BEFORE THE REVIEWS LANDED: 'nvim next.config.js' read as a dev server, because program names matched anywhere in the command line. Names now match a whole token, runners like npx are stepped over, and only subcommands match across the line. The Standards axis then found two more of the same class ('python manage.py test' was a server; 'tail -F' was not a log). 27 command lines are pinned in role.test.mjs.

THE HEADER ROW IS GONE, which criterion 1 required, and the slot-reassignment hold moved to the touch strip with it - a better home, since the SDK reports `hold` itself so the gesture needs no timer. But NOT everything the header carried found a new home, and the first version of the ADR rewrite dishonestly claimed otherwise. Corrected: the aggregate state is genuinely redundant now and was deleted; the branch identifies a channel; a workstream with no worktree is named by its label, which closed a hole where it had no identity at all; the REPOSITORY is shown nowhere, which is a real regression owned by bead -0vd.2.

PARTIAL - criterion 7, 'Tapping a pane key focuses that pane in Herdr without taking operating-system focus'. The tap sends pane.focus, which takes only a pane_id, so the plugin cannot ASK for operating-system focus. Whether Herdr raises its own window is its behaviour and was NOT verified, because doing so would have moved the focus in the developer's own running session. Asserted from the API shape, not observed. Bead -0vd.5 settles it.

Two more findings filed rather than buried: overflow panes are counted but reachable by nothing (-0vd.3), and correcting a role costs up to four holds while the key moves rows each time (-0vd.4).

198 tests, typecheck, preview, build, and streamdeck validate all pass.

The device asks for you now. Three signals raise attention: an agent waiting on input, an agent finished and not yet acknowledged, and a service that ended badly. Each marks the key that raised it and counts on its channel strip. Verified end to end against a running Herdr. All nine acceptance criteria met, one of them reworded on evidence and recorded below. Both review axes ran and both found real defects, all fixed in 6cbf1d2.

CRITERION 3 IS REWORDED, and the evidence for how took four probes against a live Herdr 0.8.0 rather than the schema.

The original wording, "a pane exiting with a nonzero status raises attention", cannot be built: pane_exited carries no exit code. Three further findings decided what replaces it.

1. A pane does not survive its own shell ending. Wrote a token on a scratch pane, sent exit 3: pane_exited fired and the pane was ABSENT from the very next session.snapshot, not flagged dead.
2. Pane tokens die with the pane; workspace tokens do not. Verified both directions on the same run.
3. Herdr emits no pane_closed for either case. Closing a pane on purpose and a pane process dying are the same event from the same path, so nothing downstream separates them.
4. A SERVICE dying is not finding 1 at all. A foreground command exiting leaves its pane alive, keeps its tokens, and emits no pane_exited - only pane_updated. I missed this on the first pass and the Spec review caught it. It matters because findings 1 and 2 had been used to claim a dead service can never have a key, which is true of the option that was rejected and false of the one that was built.

The wording is now "a service that ends badly declares it, and a clean exit does not". A workspace token sd_exit_<name> carries the exit status and the pane the service ran in. scripts/herdr-service is the wrapper that writes it: it clears the token on start, so restarting resolves the item with nothing dismissed by hand, and it declares only a real failure - 0 is clean, and 129, 130 and 143 are the developer stopping the service by hangup, Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. Reporting those would make the surface cry wolf every time a pane was closed, which is the exact failure ADR-0005 exists to prevent. The reader refuses a declared zero too, and reads it as a NUMBER, so 00 and +0 are clean as well - refusing only the character 0 would have rung the bell for a service that exited perfectly.

Option 1 from the notes is still rejected, but on findings 3 and 4 rather than 1: it would not fire for a crashing service at all, and it WOULD fire every time a pane was closed deliberately. Precisely backwards.

THE BUG WORTH REMEMBERING, found by the live run and by nothing else. Verifying end to end, the wrapper inherited HERDR_PANE_ID from the surrounding shell, so the token named a pane in a DIFFERENT workstream - and the reader believed it, stamping EXITED on an unrelated agent key. A pane id proves nothing on its own: anything can write one, and Herdr numbers panes w<n>:p<n> and reuses them across sessions. A declaration is now believed only about a pane the declaring workspace actually owns. Anything else that learns to point at a pane from a token must do the same.

ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS OF ONE FINISHED PIECE OF WORK, NOT OF A PANE. It is spent the moment the agent leaves done, so an agent that finishes twice asks twice. That pruning had to run on pane_updated and not only on a snapshot re-read: agent status arrives as a delta and schedules no read, so a mark pruned only on a re-read could have sat over the next completion indefinitely. Tapping the pane key acknowledges, because that tap already focuses the pane.

A DEFECT THAT PREDATES THIS TICKET, found while adding a preview scene. The preview and surface.test.mjs both passed process info as "process" where the reducer reads "info", and as a bare process rather than the envelope. The wrong shape type-checks in a .mjs file and delivers nothing, so EVERY pane in artifacts/xl-live-*.svg had been drawn as a shell since -4bb and those artifacts were not the evidence they were taken for. Fixed in both places; the live preview shows SERVER, TESTS and LOGS for the first time.

I STRESS-TESTED THE STRIP BUDGET BEFORE REVIEW COULD, and it caught me. EXIT was written as a required reading, but three required readings plus EXIT need 30 cells and the last channel keeps only 23 once the overflow count takes its share. Required would not have bought the space, only overrun into the count. EXIT is droppable in that one corner and ATTN still carries the fact. A test now walks every combination of waiting agents, dead services and reserved space.

WHAT ATTENTION LOOKS LIKE: three carriers, never colour alone. A word in the footer (NEEDS YOU, FINISHED, EXITED), a filled disc in the corner, and the outline. A dead service takes the danger treatment, because a pane with no agent has no state to colour an outline and the most urgent key was otherwise the faintest on the grid.

PARTIAL - nothing on the device dismisses a dead service. Restarting it under the wrapper clears the declaration, which is the action you would take anyway, but a crash left un-restarted keeps asking for the life of the workspace. Bead -0vd.6 owns it and writes down three options without choosing.

SCOPE, stated rather than hidden: the crashed-service signal only fires for services started under scripts/herdr-service. Unwrapped services degrade to silence - the same trade the hook installer makes for agents, and ADR-0005 says so.

TWO FINDINGS HANDED TO -97u, which owns the declaring half. pane.report_agent CANNOT say done - PaneAgentState is only {idle, working, blocked, unknown}, so finished is Herdr derived and only a token can carry it. And Herdr honours only the FIRST pane.report_agent for a pane; reproduced twice, an increasing seq made no difference. A hook reporting state repeatedly through that method would work once and then silently stop.

270 tests, typecheck, preview, build, and streamdeck validate all pass. Verified live: a wrapped service exiting 3 marks exactly one key, in the right workstream, on the pane it died in, with ATTN 1 and EXIT 1 on the strip; a clean restart clears both; a 130 stays silent; a pane reported blocked renders as {status: blocked, attention: waiting} with ATTN 1.

Declared attention (question/approval/finished) implemented via workspace-scoped sd_attn_ tokens, hook script, and installer. All 9 acceptance criteria met, both code-review axes clean, hooks installed for real on this machine with user approval.

Closed as a side effect of -5o6's control row: the Git and pull-request key's label is the repository name, visible without a press, on every channel including a monorepo's three checkouts. See ADR-0003's corrected note and ADR-0012.

Control row implemented: focus, git/pull-request (with repo-name identity, closing -0vd.2), and actions (prompt + armed interrupt). Both review axes clean after fixing one plugin.ts thin-adapter violation. All 11 acceptance criteria met, 341 tests, all gates green.
